Both servers killed after; netstat shows no LISTENING socket on either port.

realPageElements.note: pills and provs inside .panel-head compute flex rather than inline-flex because a flex container blockifies its items. That is CSS doing its job, not a divergence.

census.countingRule: every element carrying each class in the live DOM of the running page, both lenses, hidden and not; computedNone counts elements whose OWN display computes to none, so an element inside a display:none lens is not counted
census.reading: 40 paired values, 40 identical. computedNoneWithoutHiddenAttr is 0 everywhere, base and fixed: no element without the attribute computes display none in any of the four component classes. The rule reaches exactly the elements carrying the attribute and nothing else.

adversarialReview.q1: Could !important strand an element that show() reveals? No. show() sets el.hidden = false before clearing the inline display, and the DS screenshot shows both a pill and a prov revealed that way, rendering.
adversarialReview.q2: Could the rule hide something whose visibility is driven by a class rather than the attribute? Only if that element also carried the attribute. The census answers it by measurement: computedNoneWithoutHiddenAttr is 0 in all four classes on both lenses.
adversarialReview.q3: Is deleting .stage[hidden] safe? Measured yes, and for a reason worth recording: .stage declares no display of its own, so that patch never did anything. .stage-esc's did, and the global rule replaces it, measured to none on the real page.
adversarialReview.q4: Does the rule survive a later component rule? Measured yes, with a <style> block after the stylesheet. That is the property the card asked for and the only one the per-component form never had.
adversarialReview.q5: Does the guard actually guard? It was watched fail three times against the real file before being watched pass.
adversarialReview.q6: What does the guard NOT cover? It never renders. If the kit or a future browser changed how the cascade resolves, the tests would still pass. Recorded in the close as an unexercised path, not papered over.
